# Cache

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/cache/

# Cache

This page shows the full API of `dox_cache`, the cache behind `Cache()` in Dox.

It has `remember`, tags, atomic locks and four drivers.

## In a Dox app

`dox_core` uses `dox_cache` and exports it. There is nothing to install.
With no config, Dox has a `file` store (the default) and a `memory` store. Use it with `Cache()`:

```dart
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));
String? foo = await Cache().get('foo');

// store JSON values, so a model becomes a map with toJson()
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () async => (await Post().all()).map((Post p) => p.toJson()).toList(),
);
```

The app template has the stores in `lib/config/cache.dart`.
`lib/config/app.dart` passes them to `AppConfig(cache: cache)`.
Change this file to add a store, like Redis:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore, // CACHE_STORE in .env, default 'file'
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app_cache:'},
  },
);
```

Then set `CACHE_STORE=redis` in `.env`.

- `Cache().store('memory')` uses another store.
- `Dox().cache` is the `CacheManager` of this page. `Cache().repository` is the `CacheStore`.
- The full guide is at [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## Drivers

| Driver | What it is | Shared between isolates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memory` | a map in this isolate. Fast. Optional LRU size limit | No |
| `file` | one JSON file per key in a folder | Yes (same machine) |
| `redis` | Redis, with the [ioredis](https://pub.dev/packages/ioredis) package | Yes |
| `null` | stores nothing. Use it to turn caching off | - |

!!! warning
    Dox runs many isolates. Each isolate has its own `memory` cache.
    Use `redis` when isolates or servers must see the same data.

## Without Dox

```bash
dart pub add dox_cache
```

```dart
import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';
```

!!! note
    `dox_core` exports `CacheConfig`, `CacheManager`, `CacheStore` and `CacheLock` from this package.
    They are the same classes, so importing both packages is fine.

Make a `CacheManager` with your stores:

```dart
CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app:'},
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store
```

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| every driver | `driver`, `prefix` (default `dox_cache:`) |
| `memory` | `max_size`: the most items. When full, the least recently used item is removed. No limit when not set |
| `file` | `path` (default `storage/cache`). Each prefix gets its own sub folder |
| `redis` | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default `6379`), `username`, `password`, `db`, `tls`, `pool_size`, `max_value_bytes` (values bigger than this throw. No limit by default) |

`pool_size` is the most Redis connections one store opens in one isolate (default 10). A store uses about one, so you rarely change it.

## Basic use

```dart
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
await store.get('a');               // 1
await store.get('missing', 'none'); // 'none'
await store.has('a');               // true
await store.forget('a');
```

!!! info "No ttl means forever"
    `put` without a ttl keeps the value forever.
    A zero or negative ttl removes the key.
    `Cache()` in `dox_core` takes the ttl as a named argument: `Cache().put('a', 1, duration: Duration(minutes: 5))`.

## Remember

Get the cached value, or run the function and cache the result.

```dart
List<dynamic> posts = await store.remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 10), () async {
  return await loadPostsAsJson();
});
```

A cached value comes back as JSON. A `List` is `List<dynamic>` and a `Map` is `Map<String, dynamic>`.
So without `decode`, the type must be a raw JSON type.
For other types, pass `decode`. It turns the cached JSON into your type:

```dart
List<String> names = await store.remember<List<String>>(
  'names',
  Duration(minutes: 10),
  loadNames,
  decode: (Object? json) => List<String>.from(json as List<dynamic>),
);
```

- Many calls for the same key at the same time run the function once in one isolate. The others wait for the first.
- With `lock: true`, callers in other isolates and servers wait too. It uses a cache lock, so the driver must support locks.

## Flexible

Stale while revalidate. The value is fresh for the first time. After that it is stale for the second time.
A stale value is still returned right away, and one caller refreshes it in the background.
After both times, the value is gone and the next call waits for the function.

```dart
int count = await store.flexible<int>(
  'users',
  Duration(minutes: 5),  // fresh
  Duration(minutes: 10), // stale
  countUsers,
);
```

It takes `decode` like `remember`. The driver must support locks.

## All methods

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get(key, [default])` | the value, or the default when missing or expired. The default can be a function. It runs only on a miss |
| `getRaw(key)` | the stored JSON text, with no decode. Null when missing |
| `put(key, value, [ttl])` | store it |
| `add(key, value, [ttl])` | store only when missing. Returns true when stored |
| `has(key)` | true when the value is not null |
| `forget(key)` | remove it. Returns true when it was there |
| `flush()` | remove all items of this store |
| `many(keys)` / `putMany(map, [ttl])` | many keys at once |
| `increment(key, [by])` / `decrement(key, [by])` | change a number. A missing key starts at 0. The ttl stays |
| `forever(key, value)` | store without expiry |
| `remember(key, ttl, compute, {decode, lock})` | see above |
| `flexible(key, fresh, stale, compute, {decode})` | see above |
| `touch(key, ttl)` | set a new ttl and keep the value. Returns true when the key was there |
| `rememberForever(key, compute, {decode, lock})` | the same, without expiry |
| `pull(key, [default])` | get it and remove it, in one atomic step |
| `tags([...])` | a tagged view |
| `lock(name, [ttl, owner])` | an atomic lock |

## Values are JSON

Values must be JSON types: `Map`, `List`, `String`, `num`, `bool`, `null`. Other types throw.

- A `Map` comes back as `Map<String, dynamic>`. A `List` comes back as `List<dynamic>`.
- A stored `null` reads as a miss. `has` returns false for it.
- For a model, store `model.toJson()`, not the model.

## Tags

```dart
await store.tags(<String>['users']).put('u1', 'Ann');
await store.tags(<String>['users']).flush(); // removes only the 'users' items
```

Tags work with every driver. Old items are not deleted right away. They are just not found any more, and they go away when their ttl ends.

## Locks

Only one worker runs the code at a time.

```dart
CacheLock lock = store.lock('report', Duration(seconds: 10));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    // only one worker runs this
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

bool got = await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5)); // wait up to 5 seconds
```

- `get()` takes the lock and returns `true`, or returns `false` when someone else has it.
- `block(timeout)` tries again every 50 ms until it gets the lock or the time is over.
- The `ttl` frees the lock by itself if the worker crashes. Without a ttl, the lock stays until `release()`.
- `release()` frees the lock only for the owner that took it.
- `block(timeout, callback)` runs the callback while it holds the lock, frees the lock and returns the result. It throws `LockTimeoutException` when the time is over.
- `forceRelease()` frees the lock, whoever holds it.
- `memory`, `file` and `redis` support locks. The `memory` lock works inside one isolate only. The `file` lock is a file made with `create(exclusive: true)`. It works for all isolates on one machine. `null` throws `UnsupportedError`.

## Prefix

Every store has a `prefix` (default `dox_cache:`). It is added to every key.
Use different prefixes when two apps share one Redis database.
On Redis, a prefix with no `:` at the end gets one, so `app` does not match the keys of `app2`.

!!! info "Redis `flush`"
    `flush` deletes only the keys with the prefix. It never runs `FLUSHDB`.
    An empty prefix makes `flush` throw.

## File driver

- Each prefix has its own sub folder inside `path`. `flush` deletes only the files of that prefix.
- `add`, `increment` and `touch` take a file lock on the key, so they are safe across isolates.
- A read never deletes a file. An expired file stays until it is written again.
- `prune()` deletes the expired files. Call it from time to time, eg. in a schedule:

```dart
int deleted = await (store.driver as FileDriver).prune();
```

- Or set `prune_every` on the store to run `prune()` in the background once every that many writes. It is off by default. Each run reads every file of the store, so pick a big number, eg. `1000`:

```dart
'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'prune_every': 1000},
```

- `prune()` takes the key lock that `add`, `increment` and `touch` use, so it never deletes their new value. A plain `put` takes no lock. If a `put` writes a key at the same moment `prune()` deletes it, the new value is lost. It is only a cache miss.

## Your own driver

```dart
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver()); // or add a ready driver
```

`MyDriver extends CacheDriver`. It must implement `prefix`, `get`, `put`, `add`, `increment`, `forget` and `flush`.
Override `lock` to support locks, and `close` to close its connections.
Override `pull` to make it atomic, and `has` and `touch` to make them faster. The defaults work, but `pull` is a get and then a forget.

## Close

`cache.close()` closes the connections of every store that was built, eg. the Redis connections.
Memory, file and null stores have nothing to close. It is safe to call twice.
A store used after it is built again.

In a Dox app you do not call it. Dox closes `Cache()` stores on shutdown, in every isolate, after the open requests are done.


---

# Socket.IO

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/socketio/

# Socket.IO

This page shows how to set up Socket.IO in a Dox app with `dox_socketio`.

It can also run on its own, see [Without Dox](#without-dox).

`dox_socketio` is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart.
The official clients connect to it with no changes: `socket.io-client` (JavaScript v4) and the Dart `socket_io_client` package.
It has acks, rooms, namespaces, binary data and long-polling.
Socket.IO is the way to do realtime in Dox.

## In a Dox app

Socket.IO runs on the same port as your HTTP routes, at `/socket.io/`. You add a provider, a config, a namespace and one env key.

### 1. Install

```bash
dart pub add dox_socketio
```

### 2. The provider

The provider starts Socket.IO in every isolate. Put it in `lib/providers/`, so the generated container finds it:

```dart title="lib/providers/socketio_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/socketio.dart';

class AppSocketIoProvider extends SocketIoProvider {
  AppSocketIoProvider() : super(socketIoConfig);
}
```

### 3. The config

The config says which namespaces to serve:

```dart title="lib/config/socketio.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);
```

| `SocketIoConfig` option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | serve Socket.IO at `options.path` |
| `options` | `ServerOptions()` | see [Options](#options) |
| `namespaces` | `[]` | `NamespaceHandler` classes to register |
| `adapter` | `null` (in memory) | makes one adapter in each isolate, see [Many isolates](#many-isolates-redis-adapter) |

### 4. A namespace

A namespace handles the events of one path, like `/chat`:

```dart title="lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.emit('welcome', <String, dynamic>{'id': socket.id});
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('message', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
    event.ack('sent'); // answer the client callback
  }
}
```

See [Namespaces](#namespaces) for middleware and dependencies.

### 5. Turn it on

Add a getter for the `SOCKETIO_ENABLED` key to `lib/config/env.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
```

```bash title=".env"
SOCKETIO_ENABLED=true
```

Then run `dart run build_runner build` and `dox serve`.

### 6. Connect a client

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });
socket.on('welcome', (data) => console.log(data.id));
socket.emit('message', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'sent'
```

Use `transports: ['websocket']`. See [Many isolates](#many-isolates-redis-adapter) for why.

### Send from a controller or a service

`SocketIoProvider.server` is the Socket.IO server of this isolate:

```dart
await SocketIoProvider.server?.of('/chat').to('lobby').emit('news', data);
```

From a queue job or another program, use the [emitter](#emit-from-other-programs).

- Requests to `/socket.io/` go to Socket.IO before the router. Middleware and body reading are skipped. To log users in, see [Log in a socket](#log-in-a-socket).
- With no provider, or with `enabled: false`, there is no extra work per request.
- Need a plain WebSocket with no Socket.IO protocol? `Route.websocket(path, handler)` in `dox_core` gives you the raw socket.

### Many isolates: Redis adapter

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server.
With the default in-memory adapter, a broadcast only reaches the clients of the same isolate.
Use the Redis adapter, so a broadcast reaches clients on every isolate (and on every server).

```bash
dart pub add ioredis
```

```dart title="lib/config/socketio.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(),
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate.
/// A Redis connection can not be sent to another isolate.
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    Redis redis = Redis(); // 127.0.0.1:6379. Or Redis(RedisOptions(host: ..., port: ...))
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}
```

!!! warning "Clients should connect with websocket only"
    One websocket stays on one isolate. HTTP long-polling sends many requests, and they can reach different isolates.
    Long-polling only works with `totalIsolate: 1`, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.
    Dox logs this hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.

## Without Dox

`dox_socketio` also runs on its own, with no Dox app:

```dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.register(ChatNamespace());
  await io.listen(3001);
}
```

- `io.listen(port)` starts a native server (`dox_http_native`) on its own port. Run it in its own small program, for example `bin/socket.dart`, and put it behind the same proxy as the HTTP server.
- `io.attach(httpServer)` uses a server you already have: a `NativeHttpServer` or a `dart:io` one.
- In your own server, call `io.handle(request)` when `io.matches(request)` is true.
- `io.on('connection', (Socket socket) {...})` handles the default namespace `/` with no class.

## Namespaces

A namespace is a class. Its dependencies come in through the constructor.

```dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

  void checkToken(Socket socket) {
    if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
      throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: <String, dynamic>{'reason': 'bad token'});
    }
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

// in lib/config/socketio.dart
namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],
```

When a middleware throws a `SocketIoException`, the client gets `connect_error` with the message and the data.
Any other error is written to stderr. The client only gets `{"message": "Internal error"}`, so it can not see private text like SQL.

A client that is refused is still closed after `connectTimeout`, unless it joins another namespace.

## Log in a socket

Socket.IO gets its requests before the router, so route middleware (session, auth) does not run for it.
Use `SocketAuth` as a namespace middleware. Your function gets the handshake and gives the user, or null.

```dart title="lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart"
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[SocketAuth(findUser).handle];

  static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
    String? token = handshake.token;
    if (token == null) return null;
    return User().where('api_token', token).getFirst();
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    User user = socket.user! as User;
    socket.join('user:${user.id}');
  }
}
```

The client sends the token in `auth`:

```js
const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', {
  transports: ['websocket'],
  auth: { token: 'the-user-token' },
});
socket.on('connect_error', (err) => console.log(err.message)); // 'Unauthorized'
```

- With a user, it is kept in `socket.user`. It stays on this server. `fetchSockets()` on other servers does not get it.
- With null, the client gets a `connect_error` with the message `Unauthorized`, and `onConnection` does not run. Change the message with `SocketAuth(findUser, message: '...')`.
- `handshake.token` is `auth.token` from the client, else the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Browsers can not set headers on a websocket, so use `auth`.
- `handshake.cookie('name')` reads a cookie and decrypts it with the APP_KEY, like `req.cookie('name')`. Use `decrypt: false` for a plain cookie.
- `await handshake.session()` gives the Dox session of the client, from its session cookie. See below.
- `io.use(SocketAuth(findUser).handle)` does the same for the default namespace.

### With dox_auth

[dox_auth](../security/authentication.md#check-a-login-with-no-request) can check a JWT or the web login session for you:

```dart
static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
  // an API client or a mobile app sends a JWT
  String? token = handshake.token;
  if (token != null) return Auth(guard: 'api').userFromToken(token);

  // a browser that logged in on a web page sends the session cookie
  Session session = await handshake.session();
  return Auth(guard: 'web').userFromSession(session);
}
```

- `userFromToken` runs the same checks as `AuthMiddleware`: signature, guard, `exp` and revocation. A bad, expired, revoked or changed token gives `null`, so the client is refused. With `userCacheTtl` on, a deleted or banned user can still connect until the cache time ends, unless `forgetUser` runs.
- `handshake.session()` runs the same cookie checks as `SessionMiddleware`. A changed cookie, a cookie made with another `APP_KEY` or an expired session gives an empty session, so `userFromSession` gives `null`.
- `handshake.session()` uses `AppConfig.session`. Pass another `SessionConfig` like `handshake.session(config)`.
- The session is read once, when the socket connects. A logout later does not close the socket. Call `socket.disconnect()` yourself if you need that.
- The session is read only. Changes to it are not saved.
- With no `allowedOrigins`, or with `'*'` in it, `handshake.session()` prints a warning once.
- With the `cookie` session driver, an old copy of the session cookie still works after logout, until the session `lifetime` ends. If a logout must stop old cookies, use the `cache` session driver, like `SessionConfig(driver: 'cache', store: 'redis')`.

!!! warning "Cookie login needs `allowedOrigins`"
    A browser sends its cookies on a websocket from any website. So if you log users in with a cookie, set `allowedOrigins` to your own sites.
    Without it, another website can open a socket as your user. See [Allowed origins](#allowed-origins).

## Node.js to Dart

| Node.js | Dart |
| --- | --- |
| `socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...)` | `socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...)`, then `e.data`, `e.args`, `e.ack(x)` |
| `socket.emit('e', a, b)` | `socket.emit('e', a)` or `socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b])` |
| `await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a)` | `await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5))` |
| `socket.join(r)` / `socket.leave(r)` | the same |
| `socket.to(r).emit(...)` | the same |
| `socket.broadcast.emit(...)` | the same |
| `io.to(r).except(x).emit(...)` | the same |
| `io.of('/chat')`, `io.use(fn)` | the same |
| `socket.handshake` | `.headers`, `.query`, `.auth`, `.address`, `.token`, `.cookie(name)`, `.session()` |
| `socket.data` | `socket.data` (a `Map`) |
| `await io.in(r).fetchSockets()` | `await io.to(r).fetchSockets()` (all servers) |
| `await io.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a)` | `await io.timeout(Duration(seconds: 5)).emitWithAck('e', a)` |
| `io.serverSideEmit('e', a)` | `await io.serverSideEmit('e', [a])` |
| `io.on('e', (a, cb) => ...)` (from other servers) | `io.onServerSideEmit('e', (ServerSideEvent e) => ...)`, then `e.data`, `e.ack(x)` |

- `disconnecting` and `disconnect` give the reason in `event.data`, like `transport close` or `ping timeout`.
- Binary data: send a `Uint8List`. It can be anywhere in lists and maps.

## Options

```dart
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: <String>['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: <String>['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `/socket.io/` | the URL path |
| `pingInterval` | 25 s | how often the server sends a ping |
| `pingTimeout` | 20 s | how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone |
| `upgradeTimeout` | 10 s | how long an upgrade from polling to websocket may take |
| `connectTimeout` | 45 s | how long the client has to join a namespace |
| `maxHttpBufferSize` | 1,000,000 bytes | the biggest message. A bigger websocket message closes the connection |
| `maxAttachments` | `10` | the most binary parts in one packet. A packet with more closes that client |
| `transports` | `['polling', 'websocket']` | allowed transports |
| `allowUpgrades` | `true` | let polling clients move to websocket |
| `cors` | `null` | CORS headers for polling requests. It also checks the origin of websockets |
| `allowedOrigins` | `null` | the sites that may connect, see [Allowed origins](#allowed-origins) |

- `cors` with a list of origins: a websocket from another origin gets 403. A request with no `Origin` header (not a browser) is allowed.
- `cors: null`, or `*` in `origins`: websockets from any origin are allowed. If you log users in with cookies, list your origins.
- `*` together with `credentials: true` throws an `ArgumentError`. List your origins instead.
- Websocket compression is off. A message bigger than `maxHttpBufferSize` closes with code 1009.
- On a plain `dart:io` server (`io.attach`), the whole message is read before the size check. Also set a size limit in your proxy.

### Allowed origins

`allowedOrigins` says which websites may open a socket. Set it when you log users in with cookies.

```dart
ServerOptions(allowedOrigins: <String>['https://app.example.com']);
```

- `null` (the default): no extra check. Websockets are checked against `cors` when it is set. Dox logs a warning at start.
- `[]`: only pages of the same host can connect.
- A list of sites: the same host and those sites can connect.
- `['*']`: every site can connect.
- Other sites get 403. A client with no `Origin` header (not a browser) is always allowed.

## Many servers: Redis adapter

With more than one server process, use the Redis adapter.
Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers.

```dart
Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);
```

- `Redis` comes from the `ioredis` package.
- The subscriber needs its own connection. A Redis connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.
- It uses the format of `@socket.io/redis-adapter`. Node.js servers with that adapter can share one Redis with Dox servers.
- It reads messages in msgpack and in JSON. It writes msgpack, like the Node.js adapter.
  If your Node.js servers use a JSON parser, set `format: RedisFormat.json`.
- `fetchSockets`, `socketsJoin`, `socketsLeave` and `disconnectSockets` act on the sockets of all servers.
- Broadcasts with an ack get the acks of clients on all servers.
- Servers can send events to each other with `serverSideEmit`. Clients do not get them.
- A request waits at most `requestsTimeout` for the other servers (5 seconds by default, like Node.js).
- Long-polling needs sticky sessions, the same as with [many isolates](#many-isolates-redis-adapter). Or use `transports: ['websocket']` on the client.

### Act on all servers

```dart
// sockets of every server. Sockets of this server are `Socket`s.
List<RemoteSocket> sockets = await io.to('room1').fetchSockets();
for (RemoteSocket socket in sockets) {
  socket.emit('hello', socket.data['name']);
}

await io.to('room1').socketsJoin('room2');
await io.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

// one ack per client, from all servers. A timeout is needed.
List<Object?> answers = await io
    .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))
    .emitWithAck('ping', 'are you there?');
```

`fetchSockets` throws a `TimeoutException` when a server does not answer in time.

### Events between servers

`serverSideEmit` sends an event to the other servers. Clients do not get it.

```dart
// on every server
io.onServerSideEmit('reload-config', (ServerSideEvent event) {
  reloadConfig(event.data);
  event.ack('done'); // only when the sender waits for an answer
});

// on one server
await io.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

// wait for one answer from each other server
List<Object?> answers = await io.serverSideEmitWithAck('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);
```

When a server does not answer in time, `serverSideEmitWithAck` throws an `AckTimeoutException`. Its `responses` holds the answers that came back.
`onServerSideEmit` is also on namespaces: `io.of('/chat').onServerSideEmit(...)`.

## Emit from other programs

An emitter sends events to your clients without a Socket.IO server.
Use it in a queue worker, a cron job or a service in another language.
It writes to Redis, and every server with the Redis adapter sends the event to its clients.

Dart (for example in a Dox queue job or a CLI command):

```dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
  SocketIoEmitter emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

  await emitter.emit('news', <String, dynamic>{'title': 'hello'}); // all clients of `/`
  await emitter.to('room1').except('room2').emit('news', 'hi room1');
  await emitter.of('/chat').to('vip').emit('notice', 'for vip');

  await emitter.to('room1').socketsJoin('room3'); // sockets in room1 join room3
  await emitter.to('room3').socketsLeave('room1');
  await emitter.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

  await redis.disconnect();
}
```

Node.js, with [`@socket.io/redis-emitter`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@socket.io/redis-emitter):

```js
import { Emitter } from '@socket.io/redis-emitter';
import { createClient } from 'redis';

const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379' });
await redis.connect();

const emitter = new Emitter(redis);
emitter.to('room1').emit('news', { title: 'hello' });
emitter.of('/chat').emit('notice', 'for everyone in /chat');
```

- The emitters of other languages (PHP, Python, Go) use the same format, so they work too.
- Binary data (`Uint8List` in Dart, `Buffer` in Node.js) arrives as binary.
- The emitter does not wait for an answer. It can not know if a client got the event.
- `key` must be the same as the `key` of the adapter. Both default to `socket.io`.


---

# MCP server

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/mcp/

# MCP server

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server for the [Dox](https://dartondox.dev) framework.

It serves tools to MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, IDE agents) over the Streamable HTTP transport, from a normal Dox route.

- Tool arguments are `dox_validation` schemas: clients see them as JSON Schema, and every call is checked before your code runs.
- Session ids are signed with `APP_KEY`, so a session made on one isolate works on every isolate, and after a restart. No store is needed.
- Replies are plain JSON. No SSE stream is needed for tools.

## Install

```bash
dart pub add dox_mcp
```

## Use

Write a tool:

```dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_mcp/dox_mcp.dart';

class AddExpense extends McpTool {
  @override
  String get name => 'add_expense';

  @override
  String get description => 'Record an expense. Amount is in dollars.';

  @override
  ObjectSchema get input => v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
    'amount': v.num().positive().describe('Amount, like 12.50.'),
    'note': v.string().max(500).optional(),
  });

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> call(Map<String, dynamic> args, McpContext context) async {
    User user = context.authAs<User>();
    // ... save it
    return McpToolResult.text('Recorded ${args['amount']} for ${user.email}.');
  }
}
```

Serve it on a route. Find the user first (from a token, a header or the URL), and pass it as `auth`. `scope` ties each session to that user:

```dart
final McpServer mcp = McpServer(
  name: 'my-app',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools: <McpTool>[AddExpense()],
);

Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp/{token}', (DoxRequest req) async {
  User? user = await User().where('mcp_token', req.param['token']).getFirst();
  if (user == null) return response('Invalid token').statusCode(401);
  return mcp.handle(req, auth: user, scope: 'user:${user.id}');
});
```

A small tool can be a function:

```dart
McpTool.of(
  name: 'echo',
  description: 'Say the text back.',
  input: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{'text': v.string()}),
  handler: (Map<String, dynamic> args, McpContext context) {
    return McpToolResult.text(args['text'] as String);
  },
);
```

## Tools that take a DTO

A tool can take a `@Dto` class as its input. Extend `McpDtoTool<T>`. The rules of the DTO (like `@Length` and `@HexColor`) are written once, and `handle` gets the typed object, not a map.

Use `@Describe` on a field to explain it to the model. It goes into the JSON Schema as `description`. It does not change the checks.

```dart
@Dto()
class NewCategory {
  @Describe('The category name, like Food.')
  @Length(min: 1, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Describe('A color, like #1a2b3c.')
  @HexColor()
  final String color;

  const NewCategory({required this.name, required this.color});

  static const DtoSchema<NewCategory> schema = $NewCategoryDto;
}

class CreateCategory extends McpDtoTool<NewCategory> {
  @override
  String get name => 'create_category';

  @override
  String get description => 'Add a category.';

  @override
  DtoSchema<NewCategory> get dto => NewCategory.schema;

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> handle(NewCategory input, McpContext context) async {
    // ... save it
    return McpToolResult.text('Added ${input.name}.');
  }
}
```

- `tools/list` sends the JSON Schema of the DTO (`toJsonSchema()`) as `inputSchema`.
- The arguments are checked like a DTO in a controller, with async rules like `@Unique` and `@Exists` too.
- Bad arguments are a tool result with `isError: true`, not a JSON-RPC error. The text lists each problem, so the model can fix the call:

```text
Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool create_category: name: The name is required; color: The color must be a hex color like #1a2b3c
```

## What the server answers

| Request | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `POST` `initialize` | `200` with the server info and an `Mcp-Session-Id` header |
| `POST` a request with a valid `Mcp-Session-Id` | `200` with the JSON-RPC response (a list for a batch) |
| `POST` only notifications or responses | `202`, no body |
| `POST` with no session id | `400` |
| `POST` with an unknown session id, or one of another `scope` | `404`, so the client starts a new session |
| `POST` with an ended session id | `404`, only when `SignedMcpSessions` has an `ended` store. Without it, the id still works |
| `POST` with a body that is not valid JSON | `400` with the JSON-RPC error `-32700` |
| `POST` with an empty batch, or a message that is not JSON-RPC 2.0 | `400` with the JSON-RPC error `-32600` |
| `POST` with `initialize` in a batch with other messages | `400` with the JSON-RPC error `-32600`. Send `initialize` alone |
| `POST` with an unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` header | `400` |
| `POST` with another `Content-Type` than JSON | `415` |
| Any request with an `Origin` header that is not in `allowedOrigins` | `403` |
| `GET` | `405`: there is no server-to-client stream |
| `DELETE` with a valid session id | `200`. The session ends only if `SignedMcpSessions` has an `ended` store (see [Sessions](#sessions)) |
| `DELETE` with no session id | `400` |
| `DELETE` with an unknown session id, or one of another `scope` | `404`. An ended id also gets `404` when there is an `ended` store |

Methods: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Others get `-32601 Method not found`.

- An unknown tool is a JSON-RPC error (`-32602`).
- Bad arguments are a tool result with `isError: true` and the problems, so the model can fix them.
- A tool that throws gives a tool result with `isError: true` and the error text. `onToolError` gets the error, for logs.

Protocol versions: `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` and `2024-11-05`. A client that asks for another one gets the newest.

## Sessions

`SignedMcpSessions` (the default) makes ids like `<random>.<signature>`. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of the random part and the `scope`, with a key made from `APP_KEY` (label `dox:mcp`).

- Every isolate, and every server with the same `APP_KEY`, can check an id. Nothing is stored.
- A new `APP_KEY` ends every session. Clients start a new one by themselves.
- A signed id cannot be ended by itself. To refuse ended ids, give a cache store: `SignedMcpSessions(ended: Cache().store('redis'))`. Use a store that all isolates share (file or Redis, not memory).

For another kind of session, implement `McpSessions`.

## OAuth sign-in

`McpOAuth` lets a client sign in by itself. You give the client only the address, like `https://my.app/mcp`. The client finds the rest. This is the sign-in the MCP spec asks for: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

`dox_mcp` does the OAuth part. Your app does three things:

1. **Tokens.** Implement `McpOAuthTokens`. `issue` makes a token for a grant. `verify` gives what a token stands for (like a user), or `null`. You choose the table and how a token is revoked. Keep only a hash of the token.
2. **The consent page.** Serve it at `<issuer>/oauth/authorize`, or set `authorizePage`. It reads `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method` and `resource` from the query. The person signs in there the way your app always does.
3. **The answer.** Your page calls a route of your own, behind your own login. On yes, the route calls `oauth.approve(subject: ...)` and gives the page the address to send the browser to. On no, it calls `oauth.deny(...)`. `oauth.checkClient(...)` gives the client for the page and throws when the client or the redirect address is wrong. Then never send the browser anywhere. Put this route behind [CSRF protection](../security/csrf.md). Without it, another site can make a signed-in person say yes to a client without knowing it.

```dart
final McpOAuth oauth = McpOAuth(
  issuer: 'https://my.app',
  tokens: MyTokens(),
  codes: Cache().store('file'), // all isolates must share it
);

class McpRouter extends Router {
  @override
  void register() {
    oauth.routes(); // discovery, register and token
    Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp', handleMcp);
  }
}

Future<DoxResponse> handleMcp(DoxRequest req) async {
  Object? user = await oauth.authenticate(req); // reads Authorization: Bearer
  if (user == null) return oauth.unauthorized(); // 401 with WWW-Authenticate
  return mcp.handle(req, auth: user, scope: '$user');
}
```

On the consent page, show the redirect host, so the person sees where the browser goes. HTML-escape the client name before you print it. The client chose the name, so do not trust it.

Call `oauth.routes()` in a router with no prefix. The routes must sit at the root of the host. Clients look for `/.well-known/...` at the root, as the OAuth specs say. The discovery file also gives `<issuer>/oauth/register` and `<issuer>/oauth/token` as full addresses. Under a prefix, the routes move, but these addresses do not, so clients cannot find them.

`oauth.routes()` adds these routes:

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (also with `/mcp` after it) | Names the MCP address and the issuer. |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Lists the endpoints. PKCE `S256` only, `authorization_code` only, no client secret. |
| `POST /oauth/register` | Dynamic client registration. Nothing is stored. The `client_id` is the name and the redirect addresses, signed with `APP_KEY`. |
| `POST /oauth/token` | Swaps a code for a token. The body is a form or JSON. The code works once, for `codeTtl` (1 minute). The client, the redirect address and the PKCE verifier must all match. |

Rules:

- A redirect address must be `https`, or `http` on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`. It has no `#fragment`. It has at most 2048 characters (`McpOAuth.maxRedirectUriLength`).
- A `code_verifier` must be 43 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~` (RFC 7636). Other verifiers get `invalid_request`. A `code_challenge` must be 43 base64url characters.
- The codes live in `codes`, a Dox cache. Use a store that all isolates share (file on one host, Redis on many). Each code is taken under a lock, so two isolates cannot both swap it.
- These routes answer any origin (CORS `*`) and read no cookie. They skip the CORS list of the app.
- `issue` may throw `McpOAuthException`, like `access_denied` when a person has too many clients. The client gets it from the token endpoint.
- There is no refresh token. To revoke a client, delete its token.

## Security

- Check who calls before `handle`: the MCP route has no auth of its own. `McpOAuth` is one way to do it.
- `allowedOrigins` stops browser pages on other sites (DNS rebinding). Set it when the server runs on a local or private network.
- Keep tokens out of logs. A token in the URL ends up in proxy logs, so prefer a header when your clients can send one.

# File upload

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/file-upload/

# File upload

Accept an image from a form, check its size and type, save it to a disk, and return its URL.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`). A new app has the `dox_storage` package, `lib/config/storage.dart` and `lib/providers/storage_provider.dart`.

## 1. Set up the disk

The `local` disk of a new app saves files in the `storage` folder.
Give it a `url`. `Storage().url()` uses it to build the public URL of a file.

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storageConfig = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    /// uploads go to the `storage` folder.
    /// `url` is the public address of `Storage.route('files', ...)`.
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': '${env.appUrl}/files',
    },
  },
);
```

`APP_URL` is a new key. Add a getter for it to the `AppEnv` class:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// the public URL of this app, used in file links
  String get appUrl => 'http://localhost:3000';
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` to update `env.g.dart`.
Then add `APP_URL=http://localhost:3000` to your `.env`.

The provider of a new app sets the disks in every isolate. You do not change it:

```dart title="lib/providers/storage_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';

class AppStorageProvider extends StorageProvider {
  AppStorageProvider() : super(storageConfig);
}
```

## 2. Write the DTO

The DTO checks the file before your controller runs.

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/upload_image/upload_image.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'upload_image.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  /// jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp or bmp. Dox reads the first bytes of the
  /// file to find the real type. The file name is not trusted.
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}
```

For other file types, use `@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])` in place of `@Image()`.

## 3. Write the controller

`putRequestFile` moves the upload to the disk with a new UUID name. It does not read the file into memory.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/upload.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/upload_image/upload_image.dto.dart';

@Inject()
class UploadController {
  /// POST /api/upload (multipart/form-data, field `image`)
  Future<Map<String, String>> store(UploadImage body) async {
    // saves the file as /images/<uuid>.<ext> on the default disk
    String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', body.image);
    String url = await Storage().url(path);
    return <String, String>{'path': path, 'url': url};
  }
}
```

!!! warning "Save the file before you return"
    A file bigger than 1 MB is written to a temp file while it arrives.
    Dox deletes that temp file when the response is sent.
    So call `putRequestFile`, `store` or `moveTo` inside the controller, not later.

## 4. Add the routes

One route takes the upload. `Storage.route` serves the saved files at `GET /files/{key*}`.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/upload.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.post('/upload', (UploadController c) => c.store);
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    // GET /files/{key*}, any file of the default disk
    Storage.route('files', signed: false);
  }
}
```

`signed: false` makes every file public. Leave it out to serve only signed URLs. Then use `Storage().signedUrl(path)` in place of `Storage().url(path)`.

## 5. Register the DTOs

Dox finds a DTO in the `dtos` list of `AppConfig`. `build_runner` writes this list to `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`.
Add it once. Skip this step when your `app.dart` already has `dtos: dtos`.

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos,
  // ...
);
```

## 6. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

## Check it

Upload a PNG:

```bash
curl -F image=@photo.png http://localhost:3000/api/upload
```

```json
{"path":"/images/074aa0d0-ce21-11f1-938a-57265e28c4a3.png","url":"http://localhost:3000/files/images/074aa0d0-ce21-11f1-938a-57265e28c4a3.png"}
```

Open the `url` in the browser. The image shows.

Upload a text file. You get `422`:

```bash
curl -F image=@notes.txt http://localhost:3000/api/upload
```

```json
{"image":"The image must be an image"}
```

Send no file at all. You get `422` with `{"image":"The image is required"}`.

## Bigger files

The default limit for a `multipart/form-data` body is 100 MB. Change it in `AppConfig(maxMultipartSize: ...)`.
Set the same limit in your proxy (`client_max_body_size` in nginx).

## See also

- [Request: form data](../the-basic/request.md#form-data-file) for `RequestFile`
- [Validation: files](../the-basic/validation.md#files) for `@Image`, `@Mimes`, `@MimeTypes`, `@MaxSize`, `@MinSize`, `@Dimensions`
- [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) for S3 and signed URLs

# Pagination

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/pagination/

# Pagination

Make a list route that takes `page` and `per_page` from the query string and returns one page of rows.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`). A new app has a database (SQLite), a `User` model and a `users` table.

## 1. Write the query DTO

A DTO with `source: Source.query` reads the query string, also for `POST`.
The query key of `perPage` is `per_page`, because keys are snake_case by default.

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/list_users/list_users.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'list_users.dto.g.dart';

/// GET /api/users?page=2&per_page=10
@Dto(source: Source.query)
class ListUsers {
  @Min(1)
  final int page;

  @Range(1, 100)
  final int perPage; // query key: per_page

  const ListUsers({this.page = 1, this.perPage = 20});

  static const DtoSchema<ListUsers> schema = $ListUsersDto;
}
```

Both fields have a default, so both are optional. `@Range(1, 100)` stops a client from asking for 10000 rows.

## 2. Write the controller

`paginate()` runs one `count` query and one `select` query. It returns a `Pagination`.
A controller can return it as it is. Dox sends `toJson()`.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/list_users/list_users.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class UserController {
  /// GET /api/users?page=1&per_page=20
  Future<Pagination<User>> index(ListUsers query) async {
    return User()
        .orderBy('id', 'desc')
        .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  }
}
```

Always add an `orderBy`. Without it, the database may return the rows in a different order on each page.

Add a `where` before `paginate` to filter: `User().where('role', 'admin').orderBy('id').paginate(...)`.

## 3. Add the route

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/users', (UserController c) => c.index);
```

## 4. Register the DTOs

Dox finds a DTO in the `dtos` list of `AppConfig`. `build_runner` writes this list to `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`.
Add it once. Skip this step when your `app.dart` already has `dtos: dtos`.

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos,
  // ...
);
```

## 5. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

## Check it

With 3 users in the table:

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:3000/api/users?page=2&per_page=2'
```

```json
{
  "total": 3,
  "per_page": 2,
  "last_page": 2,
  "current_page": 2,
  "data": [
    {"id": 1, "name": "User 1", "email": "user1@example.com", "created_at": "2026-10-22T14:01:07.843207Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-22T14:01:07.843207Z"}
  ]
}
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `total` | rows that match the query, on all pages |
| `per_page` | rows per page |
| `last_page` | the number of the last page |
| `current_page` | the page you asked for |
| `data` | the rows of this page, from `toJson()` of the model |

A page after the last one gives an empty `data` list.

Bad input gets `422` before the controller runs:

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:3000/api/users?page=0&per_page=500'
```

```json
{"page":"The page must be greater than or equal 1","per_page":"The per_page must be between 1 and 100"}
```

## Change the shape of a row

Return a serializer for each row, when the model has fields you do not want to send.
`dox make:serializer User` makes `lib/app/serializers/user.serializer.dart`.
`page.data` gives the typed rows (`List<User>`):

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> index(ListUsers query) async {
  Pagination<User> page = await User()
      .orderBy('id', 'desc')
      .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    ...page.toJson(),
    'data': UserSerializer(page.data).toJson(),
  };
}
```

## See also

- [Query builder: paginate](../database/query-builder.md#paginate)
- [Validation: where the data comes from](../the-basic/validation.md#where-the-data-comes-from)
- [Serializer](../the-basic/serializer.md)

# JWT authentication

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/jwt-auth/

# JWT authentication

Let users register and log in, give them a JWT token, protect routes with it, and read the user in a controller.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`). A new app has a database (SQLite), a `User` model and a `users` table with `name`, `email` and `password` columns.
- The `dox_auth` package. A new app does not have it. Add it:

```bash
dart pub add dox_auth
```

## 1. Hide the password in the model

The token holds `user.toJson()`. Anyone with the token can read it. So the password hash must be in `hidden`.
The model of a new app already does this:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}
```

## 2. Set up the auth provider

```dart title="lib/providers/auth_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

class AppAuthProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              // APP_KEY signs the tokens. A new key logs every user out.
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              // a token stops working after this time
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

`APP_KEY` must be at least 32 bytes. `dox key:generate` makes a key of this length.
A shorter key stops the app in production, and prints a warning in development.

Dox finds the provider by itself. Run `dart run build_runner build` and it is in `lib/generated/container.g.dart`.

## 3. Write the DTOs

`@Unique` makes sure the email is not taken. It comes from `dox_orm`, so hide its `Schema` class.

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/register_user/register_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/login_user/login_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}
```

## 4. Write the controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/login_user/login_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/register_user/register_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();

    String? token = Auth().login(user);
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': user};
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth();
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/me (behind AuthMiddleware)
  User? me(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/logout (behind AuthMiddleware)
  /// By default a JWT is not cancelled on the server. The client deletes
  /// the token, and it still works until `expiresIn` passes. To cancel it,
  /// turn on revocation and call `Auth().revokeToken(req)`.
  Map<String, String> logout(DoxRequest req) {
    return <String, String>{'message': 'Delete the token on the client'};
  }
}
```

`Hash.make` makes a bcrypt hash. `auth.attempt` finds the user by `email` and checks the password against that hash.

## 5. Add the routes

`AuthMiddleware` reads the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, checks the token and loads the user from the database.
A missing or bad token stops the request with `401`.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.post('/auth/register', (AuthController c) => c.register);
    Route.post('/auth/login', (AuthController c) => c.login);

    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get('/auth/me', (AuthController c) => c.me);
      Route.post('/auth/logout', (AuthController c) => c.logout);
      // put every protected route here
    });
  }
}
```

## 6. Register the DTOs

Dox finds a DTO in the `dtos` list of `AppConfig`. `build_runner` writes this list to `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`.
Add it once. Skip this step when your `app.dart` already has `dtos: dtos`.

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos,
  // ...
);
```

## 7. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

## Check it

Register:

```bash
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register
```

```json
{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"...","updated_at":"..."}}
```

Log in with a wrong password. You get `401`:

```json
{"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}}
```

Log in and use the token:

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login | jq -r .token)

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:3000/api/auth/me
```

```json
{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"...","updated_at":"..."}
```

Without the header, `/api/auth/me` gives `401 Authentication failed`.

!!! note "The error shape"
    The `{"error": ...}` shape comes from the response handler in [Custom errors](custom-errors.md).
    Without it, the `401` body is `{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}`.

## Logout and expiry

By default the server checks only the signature, so it can not cancel one JWT. This is what you can do:

| You want | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Log out on this device | The client deletes the token. That is all `logout` does. |
| Limit the damage of a stolen token | Keep `expiresIn` short, for example `Duration(hours: 12)`. |
| Log every user out at once | Change `APP_KEY`. Every old token stops working. |
| Block one user | Delete the user. `AuthMiddleware` loads the user from the database on each request, so a deleted user gets `401`. |

To cancel one token, or all tokens of a user, turn on revocation. See [Revoke tokens](../security/authentication.md#revoke-tokens).
Or use [access tokens](../security/authentication.md#access-tokens), which you can revoke at any time.

## See also

- [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) for all options of `AuthGuard`, `JwtAuthDriver` and `AuthProvider`
- [Hashing](../security/hashing.md)
- [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md)

# Custom errors

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/custom-errors/

# Custom errors

Give your app its own exception classes, send every error in one JSON shape, and log the unexpected ones.

## What you need

- A Dox app.

## How Dox handles an error

When a controller or a middleware throws:

| Error | Status | What Dox does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an `IHttpException`, like `NotFoundHttpException` | its `code` | sends `{"code": ..., "message": ...}`. Does **not** call `report` |
| a validation error (bad DTO input) | `422` | sends the field errors: `{"field": "message"}`. Does not call `report` |
| any other `Exception` or `Error` | `500` | sends `{"code":"server_error","message":"Server Error"}`. When `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`, it sends the error text. Calls `report` |

`report` is a method of the [exception handler](../the-basic/errors.md). The response goes through the `responseHandler` of `AppConfig` last. This guide sets the shape there.

## 1. Write your own exceptions

For a quick error, use `abort(403)` or `abort(409, 'The email is taken')`. See [HTTP exceptions](../reference/http-exceptions.md#any-status-abort-and-httpstatusexception).
For errors you throw in many places, write a class.

Extend `IHttpException`. Set `code` (the HTTP status), `errorCode` (a short text for the client) and `message`.

```dart title="lib/app/exceptions/app_exception.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// 409. Thrown when the row already exists or was changed by someone else.
class ConflictException extends IHttpException {
  ConflictException({String message = 'Conflict'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.conflict;
    super.errorCode = 'conflict';
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

Throw them anywhere in a controller, a middleware or a service:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/exceptions/app_exception.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class UserController {
  /// GET /api/users/{id}
  Future<User> show(int id) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    if (user == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'User $id not found');
    }
    return user;
  }

  /// DELETE /api/users/{id}
  Future<Map<String, bool>> destroy(int id) async {
    if (id == 1) {
      throw ForbiddenHttpException(message: 'The first user can not be deleted');
    }
    User user = await show(id);

    /// 0 rows: the user was deleted after show() found it
    if (await user.delete() == 0) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'User $id not found');
    }
    return <String, bool>{'deleted': true};
  }
}
```

## 2. One JSON shape for every error

The response handler sees every response before it is sent. For an error, the content is the exception object.
Turn it into your shape here.

```dart title="lib/app/http/response_handler.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Gives every error the same JSON shape:
/// `{"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "..."}}`.
/// A validation error (422) also has `"errors": {field: message}`.
class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    dynamic content = res.getContent();

    if (content is ValidationException) {
      return res.statusCode(content.code).content(<String, dynamic>{
        'error': <String, dynamic>{
          'code': content.errorCode,
          'message': 'The input is not valid',
        },
        'errors': content.message,
      });
    }

    if (content is IHttpException) {
      return res.statusCode(content.code).content(<String, dynamic>{
        'error': <String, dynamic>{
          'code': content.errorCode,
          'message': content.message.toString(),
        },
      });
    }

    // any other exception: hide the details from the client
    if (content is Exception || content is Error) {
      return res.statusCode(HttpStatus.internalServerError).content(
        <String, dynamic>{
          'error': <String, String>{
            'code': 'server_error',
            'message': 'Something went wrong',
          },
        },
      );
    }

    return res;
  }
}
```

The last `if` gives a `500` your shape too, in every environment.
Without it, the client gets the default body. When `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`, that is the error text. It can show a SQL query or a file path.

## 3. Log unexpected errors

The `report` method of the exception handler runs for every `500`, and for errors outside a request (a future nobody awaited, a timer).

```dart title="lib/app/error_handler.dart"
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Dox calls [report] for every unexpected error (a `500`, or an error
/// outside a request). It does not run for `IHttpException` errors
/// like `404` or `422`, because those are expected.
/// One JSON line per error. Send it to Sentry or Datadog from here.
class AppExceptionHandler extends ExceptionHandler {
  const AppExceptionHandler();

  @override
  void report(Object error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
    print(
      jsonEncode(<String, String>{
        'level': 'ERROR',
        'message': error.toString(),
        'stack': stackTrace.toString(),
        'timestamp': DateTime.now().toIso8601String(),
      }),
    );
  }
}
```

## 4. Register both

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/app/error_handler.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/response_handler.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
  exceptionHandler: const AppExceptionHandler(),
  // ...
);
```

## Check it

Add a route that throws, only for this check:

```dart
Route.get('/boom', (DoxRequest req) => throw StateError('boom'));
```

| Request | Status | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/users/999` | `404` | `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"User 999 not found"}}` |
| `GET /api/users/abc` | `404` | `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"Not Found"}}` |
| `DELETE /api/users/1` | `403` | `{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"The first user can not be deleted"}}` |
| `POST /api/auth/register` with `{}` | `422` | `{"error":{"code":"validation_failed","message":"The input is not valid"},"errors":{"name":"The name is required", ...}}` |
| `GET /api/boom` | `500` | `{"error":{"code":"server_error","message":"Something went wrong"}}` |

After `GET /api/boom`, the server prints one line:

```json
{"level":"ERROR","message":"Bad state: boom","stack":"#0  ApiRouter.register.<anonymous closure> (package:my_app/routes/api.dart:41:44) ...","timestamp":"2026-10-22T14:01:12.000Z"}
```

Remove the `/boom` route when you are done.

!!! note "A URL with no route"
    A URL that matches no route is a `NotFoundHttpException` with the message `GET /nothing not found`.
    It goes through the response handler too, so it gets the same JSON shape:
    `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"GET /nothing not found"}}`.

## See also

- [Error handling](../the-basic/errors.md) for `report` and `render`
- [Response: errors](../the-basic/response.md#errors) for the built-in exceptions
- [Response: change every response](../the-basic/response.md#change-every-response)
- [Validation: the error response](../the-basic/validation.md#the-error-response)
- [Isolate: when an isolate crashes](../digging-deeper/isolate.md#when-an-isolate-crashes)

# Background work

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/background-work/

# Background work

Answer the request now and do the slow work later: after the response, on another thread, in a queue, or on a timer.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`). A new app has the queue (`dox_queue`) and the scheduler (`dox_scheduler`) set up.

## Pick the right tool

| You want | Use | Runs where | Lost when the process stops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| small I/O work after the response (a log line, a cache update) | a `Future` you do not await | the same isolate, between requests | yes |
| CPU work (resize an image, parse a big file, compute) | `Isolate.run()` | a new thread | yes |
| work that must not get lost (an email, a payment call), with retries | a queue job | the queue worker process | no |
| work every N minutes (cleanup, sync) | a scheduled task | the schedule process | it runs again at the next tick |

## 1. Work after the response

Start the future and return. `unawaited` tells the linter you did this on purpose.
An error in the future goes to the `report` method of the `ExceptionHandler` in `AppConfig`.

This file has the code of steps 1, 2 and 3:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/report.controller.dart"
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:isolate';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/jobs/build_report.job.dart';

@Inject()
class ReportController {
  /// POST /api/reports
  /// Answers at once. The work runs after the response, in this isolate.
  Map<String, String> store(DoxRequest req) {
    String id = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString();
    unawaited(_build(id));
    return <String, String>{'id': id, 'status': 'queued'};
  }

  /// POST /api/reports/queued
  /// Saves a job in the jobs table and answers at once.
  /// The queue worker (`dox queue:work`) runs it, and tries again when
  /// it fails. The job is not lost when the server stops.
  Future<Map<String, String>> queue(DoxRequest req) async {
    String id = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString();
    String jobId = await BuildReport(reportId: id).dispatch();
    return <String, String>{'id': id, 'job': jobId, 'status': 'queued'};
  }

  /// I/O work (database, HTTP calls, email) is fine here. It shares the
  /// event loop with the requests, so it must not block the CPU.
  Future<void> _build(String id) async {
    await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 2));
    print('report $id is ready');
  }

  /// GET /api/primes/{limit}
  /// CPU work runs on another thread with `Isolate.run`.
  /// The request waits for the result, but other requests are not blocked.
  Future<Map<String, int>> primes(int limit) async {
    int count = await Isolate.run(() => countPrimes(limit));
    return <String, int>{'limit': limit, 'primes': count};
  }
}

/// Must be a top level or static function with plain arguments.
/// The new isolate has no Dox, no database and no providers.
int countPrimes(int limit) {
  List<bool> sieve = List<bool>.filled(limit + 1, true);
  int count = 0;
  for (int i = 2; i <= limit; i++) {
    if (!sieve[i]) continue;
    count++;
    for (int j = i * i; j <= limit; j += i) {
      sieve[j] = false;
    }
  }
  return count;
}
```

!!! warning "Do not block the event loop"
    `_build` shares the thread with the requests of this isolate. A long loop makes them all wait.
    Put a long loop in `Isolate.run`.

## 2. CPU work on another thread

`Isolate.run` runs the function on a new isolate and sends the result back.
Pass plain data in (an `int`, a `String`, bytes) and get plain data out. Save the result in the request isolate.

`primes` above waits for the result. To not wait, combine both patterns:

```dart
unawaited(Isolate.run(() => countPrimes(limit)).then(saveResult));
```

## 3. A job that must not get lost

A future you do not await is gone when the server stops, and it does not retry.
For work that must happen, use a queue job. `dispatch()` saves the job in the database.
A worker process takes it and runs `handle()`. A failed job is tried again.

Make the job:

```bash
dox make:job BuildReport
```

```dart title="lib/app/jobs/build_report.job.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';

/// Builds a report in the queue worker.
/// Dispatch it: `await BuildReport(reportId: id).dispatch();`
@Job()
class BuildReport extends DoxJob {
  BuildReport({required this.reportId});

  final String reportId;

  /// try 3 times, wait 10 seconds between tries
  @override
  int get tries => 3;

  @override
  List<Duration> get backoff => const <Duration>[Duration(seconds: 10)];

  @override
  Future<void> handle() async {
    Logger.info('report $reportId is ready');
  }
}
```

The fields of the job (`reportId`) are saved with it. Use plain values like `String`, `int`, `bool`, `DateTime`, lists and maps.
Save an id, not a model: load the model in `handle()`.
Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add or change a job. It updates `lib/generated/jobs.g.dart`.

The `queue` method of the controller above dispatches it. `dispatch()` returns the id of the job.

A new app uses the `database` driver (`lib/config/queue.dart`).
Its jobs tables come from the migration `db/migration/..._create_queue_tables.dart`. The server runs it at start.

Start the worker next to the server, in a second terminal:

```bash
dox queue:work
```

`dox queue:failed` lists the jobs that failed every try. `dox queue:retry all` puts them back on the queue.
See [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md) for Redis, delays and all worker flags.

## 4. Work on a timer

Put the task in `lib/config/schedule.dart`. A new app has this file with an empty `schedule` function.

```dart title="lib/config/schedule.dart"
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

/// `inProcess: false`: run `dox schedule:work` next to the server.
ScheduleConfig scheduleConfig = const ScheduleConfig();

/// The tasks. `dox schedule:list` shows them.
void schedule(Schedule s) {
  s.call('cleanup', cleanupUsers).hourly();
}

/// Removes the users that were soft deleted more than 30 days ago.
Future<void> cleanupUsers() async {
  DateTime limit = DateTime.now().subtract(const Duration(days: 30));
  List<User> old = await User()
      .withTrash()
      .where('deleted_at', '<', limit)
      .get();
  int removed = 0;
  for (User user in old) {
    removed += await user.forceDelete();
  }
  print('cleanup: removed $removed users');
}
```

Start the scheduler next to the server, in a third terminal:

```bash
dox schedule:work
```

`dox schedule:list` shows each task and its next run. `dox schedule:test cleanup` runs the task now.

The scheduler runs each task once per tick, also when many processes run the schedule.
With many servers, use a Redis cache store for the lock (`ScheduleConfig(store: 'redis')`).
For a small app, you can run the schedule inside the server. See [Scheduler: run inside the server](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md#run-inside-the-server).

## 5. Add the routes

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.post('/reports', (ReportController c) => c.store);
Route.post('/reports/queued', (ReportController c) => c.queue);
Route.get('/primes/{limit}', (ReportController c) => c.primes);
```

Run `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` and `dox serve`.

## Check it

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/reports
```

The answer comes at once:

```json
{"id":"1792677668393002","status":"queued"}
```

Two seconds later, the server prints `report 1792677668393002 is ready`.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/reports/queued
```

```json
{"id":"1792677670112345","job":"9f2c4e1a7b3d5f60a1c2e3f4a5b6c7d8","status":"queued"}
```

The terminal of `dox queue:work` shows a log line with `report 1792677670112345 is ready`.
Stop the worker first, and the job waits in the `jobs` table until the worker runs again.

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/primes/100000
```

```json
{"limit":100000,"primes":9592}
```

## See also

- [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md) for drivers, retries, delays and failed jobs
- [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md) for every frequency, time zones and hooks
- [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md) for what each isolate shares, and what it does not
- [Custom errors](custom-errors.md) for the `ExceptionHandler` that gets the errors of a future nobody awaits
